key_insight: Appear2Meaning introduces a cross-cultural benchmark showing that structured cultural metadata (e.g., creator, origin, period) can be evaluated from images by combining VLM predictions with an LLM-as-Judge to measure semantic alignment with expert annotations.
problem_solved: Addresses the underexplored task of inferring structured, multi-attribute cultural metadata from images and providing a standardized, cross-cultural evaluation framework to quantify models' cultural reasoning.
method: Curate a multi-category, cross-cultural dataset of heritage images annotated with structured metadata (creator, origin, period, attributes).
Run diverse vision-language models to produce metadata predictions and use an LLM-as-Judge to semantically align model outputs with reference annotations.
Report complementary metrics (exact-match, partial-match, attribute-level accuracy) to capture fine-grained cultural reasoning performance.
impact: Provides practitioners a replicable benchmark and evaluation protocol to diagnose where VLMs fail or succeed on culturally sensitive metadata tasks, guiding model improvement and responsible deployment in cultural heritage applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: image → VLM prediction → LLM-as-Judge alignment → scoring (exact/partial/attribute).
World map or mosaic showing dataset coverage across cultures and categories.
Bar/radar charts comparing VLMs on exact-match, partial-match, and attribute-level accuracy.
Icon row: creator, origin, period, material to illustrate structured metadata types.
paper_title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
paper_authors: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Md Mohsinul Kabir, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou
